transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Mills (Redwood Product), Laura Gomez (Helix CTO), Marcus Lee (Helix ML Eng), Sophie Tran (Helix Platform Eng), Evan Park (Helix Security)

Summary: quick migration demo focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API, demo of Console (routes, rollout), Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization), and a proposed sprint plan for endpoint porting. Lots of Qs about latency/cost tradeoffs and compliance. Agreed to produce a parity CSV and schedule a poc scoping.

00:00 Alex Chen: all right hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through a focused porting sprint and show how you can map your current OpenAI / Anthropic / Together endpoints into Redwood API. we put together a short parity map and a demo of the console and optimize recommendations.
00:12 Laura Gomez: thanks Alex, excited — we need to get this off the ground quickly, timeline is Q2 for initial switch, production by Q3 if possible.
00:18 Alex Chen: got it, Q2 ramp. Priya, do you want to kick off with the parity overview?
00:22 Priya Kapoor: yeah sure, hi everyone, quick intro i'm Priya from Redwood SE. we'll start with mapping equivalencies — like model match, sampling/temperature knobs, tokenization differences, and how to handle function calling / structured outputs. tiny caveat upfront: transcription may show Together as "2gether" in some of our notes but it's Together the vendor.
00:35 Marcus Lee: great. we have a mix today — search rerank, completion-style summarization, and a chat agent using Anthropic for safety tuning. Our latency SLOs are 200ms p95 for short chat turns, but for batch rerank 1k items we're ok with 3-5s.
00:50 Priya Kapoor: perfect that helps. on the parity CSV we'll include recommended Redwood model families and quantization profiles per workload, plus estimated token cost and expected p95 latency ranges on our hosted profile.
01:05 Sophie Tran: can you show how the console handles route-level overrides? we'd like different policies for rerank vs chat.
01:12 Alex Chen: yep — i'll flip to the console. (sound of mouse) so here's the routes page, you can create a route named helix-re-rank, pin the model version, set batching window and KV cache TTL. for chat routes we show structured session affinity and kv cache persistence options.
01:29 Jordan Mills: i'll add, our optimize flags will recommend batching thresholds; for example if your rerank pattern is many short requests, we'll suggest a batching target of 64 with a 50ms batching window to save tokens without blowing latency.
01:44 Marcus Lee: that 50ms window sounds risky for our 200ms p95 chat SLO — do you have numbers?
01:50 Jordan Mills: yes we do: for chat at 50ms batching with a single GPU dedicated instance we typically see p95 in 120-180ms for <256 token turns. for safety-tuned models with longer context it's closer to 180-220ms. we'll include runbook guidance though.
02:10 Evan Park: security question — when you say hosted profile what's the data flow? is any request payload stored? what about KMS?
02:19 Priya Kapoor: good question. hosted API persists ephemeral logs for troubleshooting by default but we have options to disable retention or send logs to customer-owned storage. for Private deployments we support VPC control plane and HSM/KMS integrations; we'll send the SOC2 + encryption at rest docs.
02:36 Evan Park: okay please share the SOC2 doc and the list of supported KMS providers.
02:40 Alex Chen: noted — action item.
02:45 Laura Gomez: show us a specific mapping example — like our Anthropic safety-tuned chat -> what would that look like on Redwood?
02:52 Priya Kapoor: sure — so Anthropic Claude-internal-ish, you'd map to redwood-claude-similar or a safety-tuned redwood-compat model. in the parity CSV we'll give recommended temperature, top_p equivalents, and parameter names for system/user messages. importantly for Anthropic-style safety guards we suggest enabling the built-in moderation hook and an application-layer filter.
03:14 Marcus Lee: any tokenizer mismatch we need to handle? we saw tokenization shifts when porting from OpenAI to another vendor earlier.
03:20 Priya Kapoor: yes tokenization can change costs by a few percent; our parity sheet flags tokenization delta estimates. we also recommend a small calibration script — we can provide a python snippet that remaps prompt templates and computes token deltas against sample corpus.
03:36 Sophie Tran: about function calling — we use it heavily for structured outputs. how does Redwood handle schema enforcement?
03:42 Priya Kapoor: we have function/tool-calling compat with OpenAI-style -- you can pass schema and Redwood will try to enforce structured JSON. the console also exposes a smart validator and fallback policy to force plain-text if schema fails.
03:58 Alex Chen: quick demo will show an endpoint conversion — i'm going to paste an OpenAI curl and then show the equivalent Redwood call.
04:05 Alex Chen: (typing) so original: curl https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization...' -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","messages":[...] }'. The Redwood equivalent is a single REST call to /v1/generate with model param and a compatibility layer. note: we keep the messages array but our SDK adds structured metadata for routing and cost attribution.
04:34 Marcus Lee: do you preserve role names? we rely on assistant/system role semantics for safety prompts.
04:38 Priya Kapoor: yes we support system/user/assistant labels; we also accept Anthropic-style roles and translate under the hood.
04:46 Laura Gomez: what about streaming? our UI expects partial tokens as they arrive.
04:50 Jordan Mills: streaming is supported — we do chunked events and SDKs have client-side helpers. there is also a websocket option for lower latency streaming in private deployments.
05:02 Sophie Tran: latency in our infra is also impacted by network egress; what's common practice?
05:07 Priya Kapoor: we recommend colocating workloads in the same cloud region; if you go private on-prem we ship an appliance that runs inference on premise to avoid egress. for hosted we have regions in us-east/us-west/eu-central.
05:21 Marcus Lee: okay can we deep-dive on cost math — how do you estimate token cost given quantization and batching?
05:29 Jordan Mills: the parity CSV will show raw token rates plus an estimated effective token/second after batching and cache. e.g., quantizing to int8 may reduce GPU and therefore per-token compute cost ~30-40% depending on model. batching increases throughput which amortizes fixed kernel overhead. we'll put sample spreadsheets.
05:51 Laura Gomez: any gotchas for stateful chat and KV cache invalidation across rollouts? we've had issues where cached contexts referenced old system prompts.
06:01 Priya Kapoor: great point — we recommend strong versioning for system prompts and include a cache TTL strategy per route. Console supports canary rollouts where you route x% of traffic to a new model and warm the KV cache with synthetic sessions first.
06:20 Marcus Lee: for our rerank job we do large batch reranks overnight — curious about autoscaling for that use-case.
06:26 Alex Chen: Dedicated capacity supports configurable autoscale policies and you can set scheduled scale-ups for batch windows. there's also a burst option that falls back to hosted for short spikes if you enable it.
06:42 Sophie Tran: question about model weights residency — with Dedicated we still don't want weights in an external region. is that supported?
06:48 Priya Kapoor: Dedicated and Private let you choose region and residency; on Private you control the hardware. we'll document exactly where model weights live.
06:58 Alex Chen: switching gears — show the migration sprint plan. i'll share a high-level timeline on the screen: week 0-1 parity discovery and sample exchange; week 2-3 port 3 critical endpoints; week 4 internal poc + load tests; week 5 production cutover window.
07:18 Laura Gomez: for the sample exchange — is it enough to share a bucketing of top 3 endpoint types plus 30 anonymized examples each?
07:25 Priya Kapoor: yes that's perfect. the better the sample coverage the tighter the parity mapping.
07:30 Marcus Lee: are there any tests we can run locally to sanity-check outputs?
07:36 Jordan Mills: we'll provide a small harness that runs your samples through OpenAI/Anthropic/Together and Redwood and produces diff metrics (token delta, BLEU-ish similarity, hallucination flags, latency). it's in our repo as porting-harness.
07:51 Evan Park: legal/procurement Q — what license terms and ML IP considerations? we need to ensure no model weight exfiltration via logs.
07:58 Alex Chen: good thing to cover with legal; for hosted we have contractual protections and can disable retention. Private gives you the strongest guarantees. we'll include language in the SOW and the data processing addendum.
08:12 Laura Gomez: show me an example of the parity CSV for a rerank endpoint.
08:16 Priya Kapoor: (screen) here's a row: vendor_model=openaigpt-3.5-rerank, recommended_redwood_model=redwood-rank-8k, quant_profile=int8, batch_target=128, expected_latency_p95=3.2s, notes=use redis-backed payload cache for repeated item sets.
08:38 Marcus Lee: earlier you mentioned KV cache warming — how do we handle per-user privacy for cached context?
08:44 Priya Kapoor: TTL and namespacing. console allows per-tenant namespaces and encryption at rest; plus you can configure what fields are allowed in cache.
08:55 Sophie Tran: can the optimizer provide concrete cost savings estimates? we need numbers for a finance review.
08:59 Jordan Mills: yes, optimize runs a workload analysis and outputs potential savings as a % vs current vendor. it will highlight wins from batching, quantization, and caching. you'll get a slide-ready summary.
09:15 Laura Gomez: any feature regressions we should watch for? we've hit output format drift before.
09:21 Priya Kapoor: watch for tokenization, rounding in sampling, and small differences in beam/search defaults. the porting harness will flag format regressions and we recommend a short eval suite per endpoint.
09:35 Marcus Lee: ok let's talk about the POC environment — we want a sandbox project with limited keys and telemetry off.
09:41 Alex Chen: we can create a sandbox dedicated project for Helix with telemetry controls set to minimal retention; will be linked to your account.
09:48 Laura Gomez: commercial questions — is there a minimum commitment for dedicated?
09:52 Alex Chen: yes Dedicated usually has a monthly minimum, flexible on term. we'll include hosted and dedicated pricing in the scenarios we send.
09:59 Sophie Tran: any prebuilt integrations with our infra — we run k8s on GCP, and use cloud sql + redis.
10:05 Priya Kapoor: we have terraform modules for infra provisioning and a helm chart for private stacks; for hosted you'll just use the API and our SDKs.
10:12 Marcus Lee: let's surface a potential blocker — we rely on a custom safety model that runs post-processing on outputs; can Redwood integrate that?
10:19 Priya Kapoor: yes you can host your post-processing as a tool and call it via the function-calling pattern; or run it as a sidecar in Private.
10:28 Laura Gomez: ok last thing — can you summarize the ask from us right now?
10:32 Alex Chen: sure summary: 1) Helix to share anonymized sample payloads for 3 endpoint types (chat, rerank, summarization) by 2026-03-29. 2) Redwood to share parity CSV + code snippets by 2026-03-30. 3) Redwood to propose pricing and SOW by 2026-04-01. 4) Setup sandbox project and schedule poc scoping call week of 2026-04-06.
10:58 Marcus Lee: sounds good. one more quick Q — what's the rollback story if outputs are worse after cutover?
11:06 Priya Kapoor: rollback is straightforward: you can route traffic back to the vendor or to a previous model version. Console supports immediate traffic shift; we also recommend canary testing and live synthetic traffic to exercise behaviors before full cutover.
11:24 Sophie Tran: thanks everyone this was helpful.
11:28 Alex Chen: cool — i'll follow up on the action items. thanks all.
11:32 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and truncated words; some technical names spelled phonetically (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache", "function calling" becomes "funk shun").
